h1: CNC machine tools — CNC lathes, vertical and double-column machining centres and surface grinders
intro: CNC machine tools turn, mill, drill, bore, tap and grind the parts a fabrication shop or a machine shop makes from bar, plate and castings. NovoTech sells two lines in Canada, each on its own pages: the Dener machine tools — the premium line, built in Kayseri, Turkey — with the TTC and TTH slant-bed CNC lathes from 6″ to 12″ chucks, the TMC vertical machining centres from 33.5 to 63″ of X travel, the TDC double-column machining centres to 161.4″ and 26,455 lb on the table, and the TGH-B 450 NC surface grinder; and NovoTech's own value-line CNC machine tools, built in China to our specification — a slant-bed CNC lathe with gang tooling, BT40 vertical machining centres, BT50 CNC boring and milling machines, a horizontal machining centre and slot machining centres. Below, each line in brief and every model in one table; every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, a 1-year warranty and installation, training and parts from Mississauga, ON, Canada.

faq.q: Dener or NovoTech value line — which should I buy?
faq.a: By the work and the hours. The Dener machines are the premium line: built in Kayseri, Turkey, on stress-relieved Meehanite and slant-bed castings, with Fanuc or Mitsubishi controls, double-nut C3 ballscrews, roller guides and direct-drive spindles — the machines for two shifts and close tolerances, from a compact lathe to a 40-tonne double-column machining centre. NovoTech's value-line CNC machine tools are built in China to our specification at a lower price: the right buy for a job shop's first CNC lathe or VMC, for boring and milling large parts on a budget, or for special work such as slot machining. Both lines are installed and supported by the same NovoTech technicians, and we quote across lines so you can compare.

faq.q: Lathe, vertical machining centre, double-column or boring mill?
faq.a: Round parts — shafts, pins, flanges, bushings — go on a CNC lathe; with a C-axis and live tools the lathe also drills and mills them. Prismatic parts — brackets, housings, plates, moulds — go on a vertical machining centre up to the size of its table. Parts too long, wide or heavy for a VMC go on a double-column machining centre, whose spindle travels on a cross rail between two columns over a long table. A boring and milling machine (or a horizontal machining centre) machines several faces of a large part in one setup with a rotary table and a horizontal spindle.

Dener lathes come with the Fanuc 0i-TF Plus, Dener machining centres with the Mitsubishi M80A and Navi-Mill conversational programming — each with the other make to order; NovoTech's value-line machines are built with Mitsubishi, Fanuc or Siemens. All run ISO G-code from any CAM system; we recommend the control your programmers already know.

faq.q: What do I need on the floor?
faq.a: Three-phase power (25 to 43 kVA for the Dener lathes and TMC machining centres), shop air at 73 – 87 psi for the machining centres, and a level reinforced-concrete floor — the double-column and boring machines sit on a foundation built to the maker's drawing. We send the foundation drawing, the floor-space plan and the power requirements with the quote.

faq.q: Do you deliver, install and service in Canada?
faq.a: Yes — every machine is shipped to Mississauga, ON, Canada, unloaded, levelled and commissioned, its geometry checked, and your operators and programmers trained by NovoTech; parts for both lines are stocked or ordered through us. Every machine comes with a CSA-approved panel, 600 V standard (208 / 240 / 480 V on request) and a 1-year warranty.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
